world.bio: Solo developer in Berlin, two years into a pixel-art fishing game called Slow Water. Moved from Leipzig in 2019, worked at a mobile studio until it folded, then went freelance and got a small cultural-fund grant to build the game. I write the code, draw the sprites and compose the music badly, and I'm learning German properly so I can stop apologising at the pharmacy.
skills_assets: Godot 4 and C++ engine tooling, six years of experience
Pixel-art pipeline in Aseprite, around 900 finished sprites for Slow Water
A playable 40-minute vertical slice with a Steam page and 3,100 wishlists
Small grant from a regional media fund, tranche two paid out in June
A desk in a shared studio in Neukölln, month to month
Freelancer visa (Aufenthaltserlaubnis zur selbständigen Tätigkeit), valid until December

projects.name: Slow Water
projects.text: Pixel-art fishing game set on a lake that slowly drains over a season. Core loop works: casting, tension, a journal that fills with sketches of fish. Still missing: the second half of the lake, the weather system, save-file migration, and about half the audio. Target is a demo for the February Next Fest. Biggest blocker is that I keep re-doing the water shader instead of finishing the quest scripting.

projects.name: Fishing journal tool
projects.text: A tiny Godot plugin that turns a sprite sheet into a flip-through journal UI. I built it for myself and a couple of people on Discord asked for it. Haven't cleaned up the code. Maybe a weekend job in November if the visa mess lets me sleep.

notes.text: Third German class this week, Konjunktiv II still makes no sense to me. Frau Albrecht said my pronunciation is 'charmingly Texan'. I am from Ohio. Went bouldering after and fell off the same green problem four times.
Water shader again. Spent five hours on foam at the shoreline. Nobody will notice the foam. Closed laptop, made pasta, felt bad.

Ausländerbehörde emailed: appointment moved from Oct 2 to Oct 29. Third time. My permit runs out Dec 14. The letter says 'Fiktionsbescheinigung may be issued' which is not the same as 'will be'. Trying not to spiral. Printed all the documents again anyway.
Flatmate practised trumpet at 11 pm. The same eight bars of a Miles Davis thing. I wanted to be mad but it was getting good. Slept with earplugs.
Fixed the line-tension bug that's haunted me since May. Turned out to be a frame-rate dependency, as usual. Small win, bought a döner.
Grant report due Nov 15. Need to explain why milestone three slipped. 'Water shader' is not an answer they will accept. Draft: 'iterative visual refinement'.
Mum called. She asked if I'm still allowed to stay in Germany. I said of course, because what else do you say. Then I looked at the calendar for twenty minutes.
Playtest with four friends in the studio. They all fished for the rare carp for an hour and nobody finished the tutorial. Good sign? Bad sign? Both.
Budget check: rent 640, studio desk 220, health insurance 190, food. Grant money lasts to roughly March if I stay boring. Lost two days to tax paperwork for the Finanzamt.

messages.text: Marek: you look like death. Jonas: Ausländerbehörde pushed me again. Marek: so call them. Jonas: lol the phone line is a recording that tells you to use the online form. Marek: classic. Come bouldering, you can scream into the chalk.
Mum: Did you eat today? Jonas: Yes. Mum: What? Jonas: A sandwich. Mum: A real one? Jonas: It had cheese. Mum: Send me a photo of the fish game when you can, Aunt Carol wants to see.
Someone: your carp sprite is gorgeous, what's the palette? Jonas: 24 colours, mostly hand-picked from a lake photo I took near Leipzig. Someone: do a palette post. Jonas: maybe after the demo.

Priya: our old studio's publisher is doing a showcase in January. Jonas: I'd love to but I don't know where I'll be in January. Priya: that sounds heavy. Jonas: it's paperwork. It's only paperwork. Priya: it's your life, mate.
Elena: sorry about the trumpet. Jonas: no it's fine, it's getting really good. Elena: it's for a jam on Friday, come? Jonas: if I finish the foam. Elena: you don't need foam.

relations.about: Worries constantly; thinks the visa is a formality and keeps asking when I'm coming home for Christmas.
Studio desk neighbour, makes tower defence games, calls himself 'unlucky with publishers'.
German teacher, strict, corrects my 'der/die/das' with a small sigh.

constraints: Cannot leave the Schengen area before the permit question is resolved
No crunch work: tried it at the old studio and it broke me
Does not want to take investment that demands a mobile free-to-play pivot
Budget tight until the grant's third tranche
sensitive: Permit expires Dec 14 and the Ausländerbehörde appointment has now slipped three times; if nothing is issued he would have to leave in December
Quiet fear that the game won't sell enough to justify the two years
Anxiety that has lately woken him at 4 am
